# Adi

> Adi is an autonomous security assessment agent for **authorized** penetration
> testing — CTF competitions, educational labs, and systems the operator owns
> or is explicitly authorized to test. It is not a chatbot that suggests Kali
> commands, and it is not a vulnerability-scanner UI: it maintains a persistent
> typed model of the target (assets, services, endpoints, hypotheses,
> evidence), plans the next action with an LLM, executes real security tools
> inside an isolated Docker runtime, deterministically parses their output,
> and only treats a finding as confirmed after actual validation — never from
> a scanner alert alone.

## Key facts

- Name origin: inspired by cryptographer Adi Shamir (co-inventor of RSA).
- License: open source, hosted on GitHub.
- Core loop: build context → plan (LLM, typed action schema) → authorize
  against an explicit scope engine → execute tool in an isolated runtime →
  deterministically parse output → update the target knowledge graph →
  update hypotheses → replan.
- Safety is enforced in code: an explicit `ScopeEngine` blocks any action
  against a host outside the authorized scope, tool execution happens in a
  capability-dropped Docker container with no access to the operator's home
  directory, SSH keys, or credentials, and there is no destructive-action,
  persistence, or stealth/evasion capability.
- Works with multiple LLM providers (Anthropic, OpenAI-compatible APIs
  including OpenRouter and local inference servers) through a provider-neutral
  abstraction.
- Intended users: security students, CTF players, university labs, and
  security engineers running authorized internal/staging assessments.
- Intended NOT to be used against systems the operator does not own or is not
  explicitly authorized to test.

## الحقائق الأساسية (بالعربية)

- Adi وكيل أمن سيبراني ذاتي الحكم لاختبار اختراق **مصرَّح به فقط**: مسابقات
  CTF، مختبرات تعليمية، وأنظمة يملكها المستخدم أو لديه تفويض صريح باختبارها.
- يحتفظ بنموذج معرفي دائم عن الهدف، ويميّز بوضوح بين الملاحظة والفرضية
  والنتيجة المؤكدة — تنبيه الفاحص وحده لا يُعتبر أبدًا ثغرة مؤكدة.
- الأمان مُطبَّق في الكود عبر محرك تحقق من النطاق (Scope Engine)، وتنفيذ كل
  أداة داخل حاوية Docker معزولة بدون وصول لملفات أو مفاتيح المستخدم.
- لا يدعم أي استخدام ضد أنظمة غير مصرَّح باختبارها.
